content: Cefadroxil, marketed under the brand name DURICEF, is prescribed for the treatment of infections caused by susceptible strains of specific microorganisms in the following conditions: 1. Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): These infections must be caused by Escherichia coli (E. coli), Proteus mirabilis (P. mirabilis), or species of Klebsiella. 2. Skin and Skin Structure Infections: These infections are caused by Staphylococcus species and/or Streptococcus species. 3. Pharyngitis and/or Tonsillitis: These conditions must be caused by Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A beta-hemolytic streptococci). Important Note: Intramuscular administration of penicillin remains the only proven method for the prevention of rheumatic fever. While DURICEF is generally effective in eradicating streptococci from the oropharynx, there is no established evidence to confirm its efficacy in preventing subsequent rheumatic fever. Diagnostic and Monitoring Recommendations: Culture and susceptibility testing should be performed prior to and during therapy to ensure the causative organism is susceptible to cefadroxil. Renal function studies should be conducted when clinically indicated, as renal impairment may necessitate dosage adjustments. Antimicrobial Stewardship Considerations: To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and preserve the effectiveness of DURICEF and other antibacterial agents, this medication should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns should inform the empirical choice of therapy.
